record.paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
record.original_question: Let X be an affine scheme with coordinate algebra A and let Γ act compatibly on X and on a Lie superalgebra target, so that an equivariant map superalgebra is obtained by taking Γ-fixed equivariant maps. Generalize this setting by allowing the target to be any finite-dimensional simple Lie superalgebra, replacing the commutative coordinate algebra A by a supercommutative algebra so that X is a superscheme, and replacing Γ by a Z2-graded group. Determine the resulting representation theory in this broader equivariant map superalgebra setting.

evidence.quote: The action of Γ on X induces an action on the coordinate ring A of X. Then M = (a ⊗ A)Γ , the fixed points of the diagonal action of Γ on a ⊗ A.

(c) Superschemes and superalgebras. The equivariant map superalgebra setting of [Sav] can be naturally generalized. First, one can consider more general Lie superalgebras for the target g. For example, one could take any finite-dimensional simple Lie superalgebra (not just basic classical ones). Furthermore, one can replace A by a supercommutative algebra (in other words, let X be a superscheme) and Γ by a Z2 -graded group.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Let g be a finite-dimensional simple Lie superalgebra over k (not necessarily basic classical). Let X be a superscheme over k, with structure sheaf giving a finitely generated supercommutative associative k-superalgebra A = O(X). Let Γ be a Z/2-graded group (i.e., an algebraic supergroup) acting on X (equivalently on A by automorphisms of the supercommutative superalgebra) and acting on g by automorphisms of Lie superalgebras, in a way compatible with the Z/2-grading.

Define the equivariant map superalgebra
   M(X, g)^Γ := (g ⊗_k A)^Γ,
the subsuperalgebra of Γ-fixed points of the diagonal Γ-action on the Lie superalgebra g ⊗_k A (with bracket [x ⊗ a, y ⊗ b] = (-1)^{|a||y|}[x,y] ⊗ ab).

Develop the finite-dimensional irreducible representation theory of M(X, g)^Γ in this generalized setting: classify (up to isomorphism) the finite-dimensional irreducible M(X, g)^Γ-modules, describe them via evaluation-type constructions at (super)points of X, and determine when two such constructions yield isomorphic modules. In particular, extend the existing classification (known when g is a finite-dimensional basic classical Lie superalgebra, A is an ordinary finitely generated commutative algebra, and Γ is an ordinary finite group acting freely on the maximal spectrum of A) to the case where g is any finite-dimensional simple Lie superalgebra, A is supercommutative, and Γ is a Z/2-graded group.
artifact.status_search_result: This is posed as an open direction for future work in the equivariant map (super)algebra literature. A general classification of finite-dimensional irreducible representations in this fully super setting (arbitrary finite-dimensional simple Lie superalgebra target, supercommutative coordinate superalgebra, and Z/2-graded acting group) does not appear to have been established; partial results exist for basic classical g with ordinary commutative A and ungraded Γ. Status appears to remain open.
